sections.section_name: Section B - Very Short Analytical Concepts

questions.question_text: Define a double league tournament and state its mathematical formula for calculating the total number of structural matches. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: In a double league tournament, every participating team plays against every other team exactly twice. The total matches are calculated using the formula $N(N - 1)$, where $N$ is the number of teams.

questions.question_text: Differentiate structurally between active flexibility and passive flexibility in physical education. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Active flexibility is executing a movement using only one's internal muscular strength, while passive flexibility achieves joint motion with external assistance, such as a partner or gravity.

questions.question_text: State the standard WHO classification of an adult athlete presenting a calculated Body Mass Index (BMI) of 28.5. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: An adult with a BMI of 28.5 falls strictly into the 'Overweight' category, as it lies within the 25.0 to 29.9 standard WHO measurement metric bracket.

questions.question_text: What is a sprain structurally, and which anatomical tissue does it primarily affect during a sports injury? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A sprain is a severe structural overstretching or tearing of ligaments, which are the fibrous connective tissues that strictly anchor bones together at a joint capsule.

questions.question_text: List two absolute essential structural safety gear requirements mandated for participating in paragliding. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Paragliders must critically utilize a certified aerodynamic helmet and an emergency reserve parachute system attached directly to the main structural harness for mid-air fail-safes.

sections.section_name: Section C - Short Explanatory & Anatomical Tiers

questions.question_text: Explain the specialized concept of 'Special Seeding' in structural knockout tournament fixtures. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Special seeding is a privileged placement granted to exceptionally strong teams (usually defending champions). Instead of participating in initial rounds, these seeded teams directly enter the structural quarter-finals or semi-finals, preventing early elite eliminations.

questions.question_text: Describe the anatomical procedure for measuring waist-to-hip ratio and explain its clinical significance in health evaluations. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: It is measured by dividing the circumference of the waist at its narrowest point by the circumference of the hips at their widest. It clinically indicates visceral fat distribution, strictly highlighting risks of metabolic and cardiovascular disorders.

questions.question_text: Outline the full 'P.R.I.C.E' structural protocol for managing a recent sports-related muscle strain injury immediately post-impact. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The protocol dictates Protection (shielding from further harm), Rest (ceasing activity), Ice (applying cold to reduce swelling), Compression (wrapping to control fluid buildup), and Elevation (raising the injured limb above heart level to drain fluids).

questions.question_text: Explain how muscular strength fundamentally differs from muscular endurance, providing one practical structural exercise example for each. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Muscular strength is the maximum absolute force a muscle can generate in a single effort (e.g., one-rep max heavy deadlift). Muscular endurance is the ability to sustain repeated contractions over time (e.g., executing fifty continuous push-ups).

questions.question_text: Discuss the core psychological and structural objectives of including extreme adventure sports within standardized school physical education programs. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Adventure sports build structural resilience, enhance risk-management cognition, and foster deep environmental awareness. Psychologically, overcoming extreme natural obstacles rapidly develops leadership, self-confidence, and team-based survival dependencies.

questions.question_text: Read the following tournament data context: A sports coordinator draws up a competitive league framework for 11 participating teams using a standard Knockout Fixture layout. Compute the total number of matches required and determine the exact allocation of 'Byes' across the upper and lower halves of the draw. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Total matches required equals $N - 1 = 11 - 1 = 10$. The next highest power of two is 16, so total Byes $= 16 - 11 = 5$. The lower half receives $\frac{NB + 1}{2} = \frac{5 + 1}{2} = 3$ Byes, while the upper half layout holds exactly $\frac{NB - 1}{2} = 2$ Byes.

questions.question_text: A 16-year-old athlete has a recorded body mass of 75 kg and a structural height of 1.70 m. Calculate his Body Mass Index (BMI). Based on standard metrics, categorize his structural fitness bracket and suggest one dietary or training adjustment. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: BMI equals $75 / (1.70 \times 1.70) = 75 / 2.89 = 25.95$. This places the athlete structurally in the 'Overweight' bracket. A recommended adjustment is increasing daily aerobic cardiovascular training while maintaining a slight caloric deficit to optimize body composition.

questions.question_text: During a school hockey match, a player falls awkwardly, resulting in a visible bone displacement at the shoulder joint without skin penetration. Identify this specific sports injury type and list immediate structural first-aid responses prior to medical transport. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: This is a closed joint Dislocation. First aid requires absolute structural immobilization of the shoulder using a specialized sling or splint in the position found. Do not attempt to relocate the bone, apply ice to numb pain, and arrange immediate professional medical transport.

sections.section_name: Section E - Long-Form Structural Rules & Training

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the concept of 'Health-Related Physical Fitness' versus 'Skill-Related Fitness'. Break down three distinct anatomical components of health-related fitness and explain how they structurally benefit an individual's longevity and quality of life. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Health-related fitness ensures disease prevention and bodily functionality, whereas skill-related targets athletic performance. Three health components include: Cardiorespiratory endurance (strengthens heart/lungs to delay fatigue), Body composition (optimizes fat-to-muscle ratios to prevent metabolic disorders), and Flexibility (maintains joint elasticity, drastically reducing structural injuries and mobility loss in advanced age).

questions.question_text: A physical education teacher must organize an intramural basketball tournament for 7 teams. Draft the step-by-step mathematical logic to construct a cyclic method league fixture, detailing the total number of structural rounds, total matches, and rotational mechanics. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: For $N=7$ (odd), the formula for total matches is $N(N-1)/2 = 7(6)/2 = 21$ matches. The number of rounds equals $N$, so there are 7 structural rounds. In the cyclic layout, a 'Bye' is permanently fixed at the top right of the grid, while the remaining 7 teams rotate in a continuous clockwise direction every round.

questions.question_text: Analyze the critical environmental and physiological risks associated with high-altitude mountaineering. Detail the required acclimatization process and necessary structural safety protocols needed to prevent conditions like acute mountain sickness (AMS) in extreme athletes. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: High altitude introduces severe oxygen deprivation (hypoxia) and extreme cold, risking hypothermia and Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS). Acclimatization requires gradual structural ascent, adhering to the 'climb high, sleep low' rule to allow physiological RBC proliferation. Safety protocols dictate carrying supplemental oxygen, hydration tracking, thermal layering, and immediate rapid descent at the first neurological signs of AMS.
